name: Unified web workspace
flow: Prep, scan, edit and reports in one workspace
All data operations use the canonical API
Registered label file returns to the workspace, then the printer
Room configuration, sessions and audit history remain in one authoritative database
functional_difference: One application and one shared workstation expose every role's screens.
benefit: One installation and one navigation model.
risk: The shared workstation can interrupt every task; a busy room screen may expose too many controls.
backend_change: No required domain change. Role authorization is enforced by the existing service.
trial_actions: Fail the shared client and preview each task
Print registered labels
Compare this arrangement with role-specific apps

name: Three role-specific web apps
flow: Prep and label app registers identities
Room app submits explicit movements
Audit app submits corrections and reads reports
Each app uses the same canonical API and database
Registered label file goes from prep app to printer
functional_difference: Prep/printing, scanning and audit work have separate applications and release cycles.
benefit: Each role gets a focused surface without duplicating records.
risk: Three deployments need consistent API contracts and permissions.
backend_change: No separate database required. Keep compatible authenticated API contracts.
trial_actions: Fail only the room app
Preview supervisor correction while scanning is unavailable
Disconnect the central service link

name: Local Pi kiosk + staff portal
devices: Pi touchscreen with locally installed interface
flow: Staff portal prepares, prints, corrects and reports
Local Pi interface captures scanner input
Both clients call the canonical central API
Confirmed movements and corrections use the same authoritative database
Optional durable capture is an unconfirmed extension, not ordinary success
functional_difference: The room screen can cold-start locally while staff work remains in a separate web portal.
benefit: A network failure still leaves a usable local unavailable screen.
risk: A local screen is not a functioning database connection; installed assets must be updated.
backend_change: None for online use. Optional offline capture needs reconciliation and asserted-device-time provenance.
trial_actions: Disconnect the central link and inspect local-screen status
Preview an unavailable scan
Enable the optional capture extension and compare its unconfirmed outcome

name: Headless scanners + supervisor console
devices: Fixed scanner appliance with IN/OUT controls and status indicator
flow: Prep desktop registers and prints labels
Appliance submits movement requests through an API
Physical controls or command cards choose whole-stack versus specimen action
Supervisor console handles exceptions and reads reports
All writes still use the same authoritative service and database
functional_difference: Routine scanning has no browser or touchscreen; exception editing happens elsewhere.
benefit: Few controls at the door; a failed scanner does not disable supervisor work.
risk: Partial selection and detailed errors need clear command-card/status conventions or a nearby console.
backend_change: Existing movement API plus device authentication; no database credentials on appliances.
trial_actions: Fail the scanner appliance
Preview a correction from the supervisor console
Disconnect the API and check that the indicator cannot claim success

name: Native print utility + web tools
flow: Native utility reviews prep data and requests canonical identities
API supplies registered label artifacts
Utility sends label files through the local printer driver
Room scanner and audit browser use the same API
Cached registered files can reprint without creating new records
functional_difference: Printing integrates with the staff PC's driver while scanning and audit remain web applications.
benefit: Better local printer integration and reprinting of already registered files.
risk: Native packaging and updates become another maintenance task; cached files must preserve identity/version.
backend_change: Use existing prep/label endpoints. Native clients call the API rather than receiving database credentials.
trial_actions: Disconnect the central link and reprint a saved registered file
Compare cached reprinting with blocked new movement
Fail only the room scanner

name: Managed handheld + desktop review
flow: Desktop prepares, prints, corrects and reports
Handheld identifies room and selected specimens
Installed app submits movements to the canonical API
Authoritative sessions and audit history remain on the server
Optional local capture requires later reconciliation
functional_difference: The scanner moves with the worker; printing and audit editing stay on a desktop.
benefit: Selection and scanning can happen beside the rack.
risk: Device charging, room binding and managed updates need explicit procedures.
backend_change: Existing API plus handheld/device authentication. Queueing is a separate optional extension.
trial_actions: Fail the handheld while desktop review remains available
Preview a normal scan
Compare optional unconfirmed capture during a link failure

name: Operator requests + approval portal
flow: Prep app registers and prints labels
Operator room app submits normal movements
Operator submits a correction request without altering sessions
Supervisor approval portal authorizes the revision
Canonical service records the request, decision and resulting correction
functional_difference: Operators can describe mistakes immediately, but a separate approval step applies corrections.
benefit: The exception and its approval are attributable without exposing direct editing to operators.
risk: Pending corrections need ownership and may delay usable audit records.
backend_change: Add durable correction requests and approval/rejection workflow; canonical session updates occur only on approval.
trial_actions: Submit a correction request and inspect the unchanged record
Approve the pending request
Fail the room app while the approval portal remains available

name: Site server + central reporting
flow: Site clients use the site authoritative API
Site database stores identity, room configuration, sessions and audit history
Registered labels return to the site printer
A one-way delivery supplies a central reporting copy
Central reports show provenance and lag; they do not accept competing movement writes
functional_difference: A WAN outage can leave site-local recording operational while central reporting becomes historical.
benefit: Room operations depend on the site network rather than the external reporting link.
risk: The site server requires operational ownership; central copies must expose freshness and avoid dual writers.
backend_change: Site-host the canonical service and add read-only reporting delivery with globally unique identities and provenance.
trial_actions: Disconnect the site-to-central link and preview a confirmed local scan
Open the historical central report
Fail the authoritative site database and compare the resulting write failure
